findings.title: Worker mock cannot detect a wrong filter request
findings.why_it_matters: The calculation UI tests pass even if the workbench sends stale or incorrect selections to the worker: the fake worker saves only the request ID and returns the same number for every input. A user could see results for different selections than the ones shown on screen while the domain and UI tests both remain green. Capture the posted input and assert it after a selection change, then return a result derived from that input so the UI result assertion exercises the connection.
findings.suggested_fix: Have WorkerPort.postMessage record the full input; in a UI test, change a position or rule before calculating, assert the posted input, and generate a small input-sensitive result for the displayed-output assertion.

findings.title: History view tests never assert displayed data
findings.why_it_matters: All six history displays are in the requested scope, but the UI tests only verify navigation, retained range settings, and adding a rule. A rendering regression in frequency counts, heatmap positions, category percentages, line values, or detail rows would pass the suite even though users rely on those numbers to choose filters. Drive a small known CSV through the import UI and assert representative values across the six tabs and the selected range.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a history component test using a short CSV with distinct known digits and metrics; select each of the six tabs and assert its visible data, including a changed observation range and position.
